research_rationale: EO 12785 of December 26, 1991 (Extending the President's Education Policy Advisory Committee), read in full in the held Federal Register text (56 FR 67451, Federal Register of December 30, 1991; machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF). Under the owner's strike-and-insert ruling (2026-10-21) an amendment normally continues until its parent ends; this amendment's only content is the Committee's run to December 31, 1992, so its first end is that date, recorded inclusive as the owner's until-date ruling (2026-10-21) directs; the exclusive reading (the Committee ends when that day begins) is the alternative a reviewer should see. research_rationale: EO 13561 of December 22, 2010 (Adjustments of Certain Rates of Pay; 75 FR 81817, Federal Register of December 29, 2010) sets pay rates for the statutory pay systems, the Senior Executive Service, executive, legislative and judicial salaries, uniformed services, locality-based comparability payments and administrative law judges by attached schedules, and in its section 8 supersedes its predecessor. Its section 7 makes Schedule 8 effective January 1, 2011 and the other schedules effective on the first day of the first applicable pay period beginning on or after January 1, 2011. Section 8 reads "Executive Order 13525 of December 23, 2009, is superseded." It is a self-executing supersession with no deferred effective date, performed when EO 13561 took effect on signing (2010-12-22); the project records the same kind of clause that way elsewhere. That clause's first end is 2010-12-22. Every other clause ends with the supersession of this order by EO 13594 of December 19, 2011 (76 FR 80191, Federal Register of December 23, 2011), whose section 8 reads "Executive Order 13561 of December 22, 2010, is superseded." That sentence is an express supersession of the whole order and carries no effective-date qualifier of its own; EO 13594 section 7, which gives its own schedules the effective dates January 1, 2012 (Schedule 8) and the first day of the first applicable pay period beginning on or after January 1, 2012 (the other schedules), speaks only of the "other schedules contained herein" and does not defer section 8. The supersession therefore took effect on signing, 2011-12-19, and that is the first end of the schedule clauses. Disclosed alternative reading: the schedules of EO 13561 continued to govern pay until the new schedules took effect (January 1, 2012 for Schedule 8; the first day of the first applicable pay period beginning on or after January 1, 2012 for the others, a date the held sources do not give). The lead-in of EO 13594 recites that Public Law 111-322 freezes certain pay schedules for civilian Federal employees at 2010 levels through 2012, which accounts for continuity of rates between the two orders without any continuing force in EO 13561. A by-number search of the held order texts for EO 13561 finds this order's own text and EO 13594 (Federal Register and American Presidency Project copies); EO 13594 is the earliest held instrument naming this order, and no earlier revocation, supersession or amendment is held. The alternative reading that the schedules governed pay until the new schedules took effect is disclosed in the rationale; the later order's section 7 dates its own schedules and does not defer its section 8.

research_rationale: Executive Order 7845 of March 21, 1938 prescribes regulations on annual leave for civilian officers and employees of the United States, the District of Columbia and covered corporations under section 7 of the act of March 14, 1936 (49 Stat. 1161). The held text is the Federal Register print as machine-extracted from the official PDF (3 FR 715 to 717). The dossier inventory is corrected in four ways: an enacting-paragraph clause is added; section 9 and section 19(e) are each split at a page break so the Federal Register page header and table of contents are not carried inside a clause; section 19(e) is separated from section 19(f), which the machine segmentation merged because the held text prints (f) as "if)"; and Part headings are trimmed from the ends of sections 1(i) and 18. Sections 20 through 22 are retained. Executive Order 8384, signed 1940-03-29, states that it supersedes Executive Orders No. 7845, No. 7879 and No. 8226 and is effective as of March 2, 1940, so the continuing regulatory clauses end on 1940-03-02; its sections 6 and 9 are effective as of July 1, 1936 for leave adjustments, which is disclosed for sections 6 and 9. Section 20 (ratification and revocation of inconsistent regulations), section 21 (effective date and supersession of Executive Order 7409) and section 22 (publication) are one-time commands exhausted by performance, recorded with their performance dates rather than the later supersession. Section 6 was restated by Executive Order 7879 (signed 1938-05-09, effective as of January 1, 1938) and section 15 by Executive Order 8226 (signed 1939-08-24, effective as of June 30, 1939); both are later events recorded at their stated effective dates, with before-and-after text, not ends. Conflict on Executive Order 8384: the Office of the Federal Register note on this order reads 'EO 8384, March 29, 1940 (in part)', which the dossier flags as a whole-and-partial conflict. The held text of section 21 of Executive Order 8384 says 'This order shall supersede' Executive Orders No. 7845, No. 7879 and No. 8226 without limiting words, and carves out only the effective dates of its own sections 6 and 9; the supersession is read as whole. The dossier's chain also lists EO 7880 as a section 6 amendment; the held page for EO 7880 is the same Federal Register page (3 FR 1075) that carries EO 7879, and EO 7880 amends section 9 of EO 7846 (sick leave), not this order, so it is not a later event of this order.
savings_reason: Executive Order 8384 supersedes the order and re-prescribes the annual leave regime. Its section 21 proviso caps the total leave credited as a result of adjusting leave on the basis of the amended regulations at the amount authorized to be accumulated by law; it does not itself state that leave credits earned under EO 7845 are carried forward. Leave accrued and used under EO 7845 before the supersession is an accrued consequence of a performed regime, and no held source shows a loss of that leave, so the savings state records that the effects of the superseded regulations accrued before 1940-03-02 and the later order governs thereafter.
conflict_resolutions: {"FULL_AND_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT":"The Office of the Federal Register note on EO 7845 reads 'EO 8384, March 29, 1940 (in part)'. The held text of EO 8384 section 21 states that the order 'shall supersede' EO 7845, EO 7879 and EO 8226 without limiting words; only the effective dates of its own sections 6 and 9 are carved out (July 1, 1936, for leave adjustments). The text supports a whole supersession of EO 7845, effective as of March 2, 1940, and the note's 'in part' is read as the editorial reflection of the saving carve-out for sections 6 and 9, which is disclosed in the reasons for those two clauses."}

research_rationale: EO 9278 (signed December 4, 1942; F.R. Doc. 42-12921, filed December 5, 1942) was read in full in the registered held text (machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF, grade original_representation_unverified, under jobs/fr-originals); the heading, body, signature, date and filing line were read; page images were not compared. Under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935 and the act of February 11, 1936 the President appoints Benjamin W. Thoron, Director, Division of Territories and Island Possessions, Department of the Interior, as Administrator of the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration, vice Guy J. Swope, resigned, to serve without additional compensation and to exercise the functions conferred on the Administration and Administrator by Executive Orders 7057, 7180 (as amended by 7554) and 7689, and amends those orders accordingly. The order is a one-time appointment and amendment, complete when issued on 1942-12-04; Thoron's later service is a historical consequence of the appointment, and the functions he exercised are conferred by the earlier orders, which keep their own lifecycles. A later order, EO 9618 (September 19, 1945), appoints a successor 'vice Benjamin W. Thoron, resigned', showing the service had ended by resignation on a date before then that no held source gives; that is recorded as a later event, not an end. Applying the owner ruling of 2026-10-28, the appointing act is recorded as exhausted by performance and the surviving appointment is separated from it. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification.
savings_reason: The appointment, the service rendered under it and the amendment of EOs 7057, 7180, 7554 and 7689 are accrued effects of the performed order. The functions of the Administrator continue, if at all, under those earlier orders and the cited statutes, not under EO 9278.
earlier_end_check: A ripgrep scan run on 2026-11-04 over every .txt file under jobs/ (jobs/clause-drafts excluded) for the number 9278 followed by 'of' or 'dated' and a month name, together with the Cruden number-citation lookup in the packet LOOKUPS.md, found no held text citing EO 9278 other than the Federal Register pages that print it (EO 9280 and its adjacent pages). The packet chain lists five later orders: EO 9288 and EO 10018 transfer tracts of land to the Secretary of Agriculture, and EO 9618, EO 9901 and EO 10468 appoint successor Administrators; none revokes or supersedes EO 9278. The machine searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog were read for coverage (all three marked complete, no scope note) and are recorded as leads, not as independent review. The jobs/namier person-name search lists five name-match texts for Thoron: EO 9279 (an index entry), EO 9280 (its file prints this order's page), EO 9617 (its file prints EO 9617, EO 9618 and EO 9619, 10 FR 11929-11931, not this order's page), EO 9618 (the only one that appoints the successor, 'vice Benjamin W. Thoron, resigned') and EO 9619 (it amends Schedule A of the Civil Service Rules and appoints no one; its file names Thoron only because it reprints EO 9618). None ends the order.
scope_check: One operative scope (EO:9278#whole): the appointment sentence, including the service terms, the direction to exercise the functions conferred by EOs 7057, 7180, 7554 and 7689, and the sentence amending those orders. The signature block carries no command. The machine inventory of one scope is complete.
independent_command_check: The direction to exercise the earlier orders' functions and the amendment sentence are part of the same one-time appointment act; the underlying functions are conferred by the earlier orders and are not made independent commands of EO 9278.
savings_check: No savings clause. The appointment and amendment are accrued effects; later orders' continuation of the Administration is not a continuation of this order.

research_rationale: Executive Order 9938 (13 FR 1555, Federal Register of March 24, 1948; PDF pages 1-3 of the held machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF) is headed Oregon, Revoking Executive Order No. 9544 of April 25, 1945, Authorizing the Secretary of War to Assume Control of a Certain Airport. Identity: number, subject and date agree with the census register row (1948-03-22). The held text prints the order in pieces. The order begins on PDF page 1 and breaks at "the lease shall again be operative and" with the note that it continues on page 1557. The closing words are printed on PDF page 3 as "in full force and effect upon the signing" followed by "of this order." and the signature of Harry S. Truman, and the line "March 22, 1948." with the Federal Register filing line (FR Doc. 48-2642, filed March 22, 1948, 4:26 p.m.) is printed further on PDF page 3 after unrelated table-of-contents matter, which is how the page layout scrambled the page. The American Presidency Project mirror text of the order agrees with the Federal Register pieces, joins them into one sentence and gives March 22, 1948; the Federal Register text is the registered source and is the one quoted here. Inventory (corrected from the dossier's single clause, which ran across unrelated table-of-contents and other documents): two clauses, each a contiguous span of the held text. The first (characters 3421 to 4233) is the authority recital, the revocation of Executive Order No. 9544 of April 25, 1945 as to the described Oregon airport lands (1,520 acres), and the statement that the lands are included in a twenty-year lease to the City of Redmond from March 12, 1942, beginning the intention that the lease again be operative. The second (characters 13002 to 13060) is the closing of that sentence, "in full force and effect upon the signing" of the order. Ending: the revocation says Executive Order No. 9544 "is hereby revoked" and the closing words tie the lease's reactivation to "the signing of this order"; neither has a deferred effective date, so both were performed on signing, March 22, 1948 (the date printed in the held Federal Register text, which agrees with the filing date), and each clause is exhausted by performance on that date. The machine own-term candidate of 1962-03-12 is the end of the Redmond lease described in the order; it is a fact about the lease, not an end of the order's revocation, so it is not used. Searches: a by-number search of the held order texts for EO 9938 returns 0 matches, so no held later order cites it; the Federal Register disposition-note, U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report no hit naming this order. The surviving consequence is that Executive Order No. 9544 stays revoked and the lease operates again; that consequence is not a command left to end. Searches: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts) were chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no scope warning.

earlier_end_check: No earlier end exists: both commands were performed when the order was signed, March 22, 1948. The effective moment is stated in the held Federal Register text ("the signing of this order"); the held pieces are printed out of order but are all present, and the date line "March 22, 1948." agrees with the filing line. The only later date in the packet, 1962-03-12, is the end of the Redmond lease, not of the order.
scope_check: Two clauses covering the whole order: the revocation with the lease recital (printed on the first PDF page) and the closing words of the same sentence (printed on the third). The signature and date lines carry no command. The dossier clause is replaced by these two spans.
independent_command_check: The only command is the revocation. The statement about the lease records an intent about an existing lease between other parties and creates no continuing duty of the order.
